gap: No result ChatGPT got states, across brands, that the "60 seconds" quoted for Vyncs Basic 4G+ is a GPS sample rate whose points reach the account in 3-minute batches (Vyncs's own footnote), while Bouncie says it records and sends every second, and that closing the gap means Vyncs Pro at $165.98 in year one, against $107.40 for Spytec Pulse OBD on its annual plan.
standout_why: Compared against rottenwifi.com (cited), vyncs.com/pricing.aspx (cited), bouncie.com/pricing (cited), hotairtag.com, allinsider.net, gpstrackerreviews.net, tagandtether.com and vyncs.com's comparison page. Every third-party page gives Vyncs as a flat 60-second tracker (rottenwifi: "samples GPS data every 60 seconds"; allinsider: "about every 60 seconds on the base plan"; gpstrackerreviews: "60 second refresh on the base plan"; tagandtether: "every 60 seconds"), and none mentions the 3-minute batching or the $30 and $20 upgrade prices. But the cited Vyncs pricing page carries the footnote and the upgrade table itself, and hotairtag already prints 1-year and 3-year totals for Bouncie ($206 / $437) and Spytec Pulse OBD ($107 / $322). So rivals hold the parts; what is new is the side-by-side normalisation and the correction of the roundups. Spytec's own update interval could not be read (store returned HTTP 429), which leaves the table's key column empty for the product Dealectric lists. winchinsider.com (TLS error) and roadandtrack.com (blocked) could not be opened.
decides: It confirms Spytec Pulse OBD on cost but not on update speed. On cost, Spytec's annual plan is the lowest of the three in year one ($107.40, against $145.98 for Vyncs Basic and $205.79 for Bouncie) and stays lowest through year three ($322.20, $345.96, $437.39). It changes the Vyncs line: Basic's $99.99 a year buys 3-minute uploads, and Basic plus both speed upgrades ($195.98 in year one) costs more than Vyncs Pro ($165.98), which includes them. A shopper who wants second-by-second live tracking is pointed to Bouncie on Bouncie's own claim. The page cannot say where Spytec sits on update interval until that figure is sourced.

findings.source_title: Vyncs pricing (with the Spytec and Bouncie sources listed in the rows above)
findings.note: Footnote that is the finding: the three makers' "real-time" figures are not the same measurement. Vyncs quotes a sample rate and uploads in batches; Bouncie quotes record-and-send; Spytec's interval was not read. Vyncs Basic renews $7.41/year below Spytec's annual plan (99.99 against 107.40), so the $38.58 year-one gap closes only in year seven (cumulative $745.92 against $751.80). Bouncie figures rest on rottenwifi's reported price.

Bouncie device and monthly price on Bouncie's own site today: bouncie.com/pricing, bouncie.com and bouncie.com/location rendered no dollar amounts in the fetch, and no help-centre price article turned up. The $89.99 + $9.65/month figure comes from rottenwifi and Vyncs's comparison page.
